name: Daily Stand-up
one_liner: Sixty to ninety seconds each: alignment on the goal, blockers, confidence.
purpose: The Daily Stand-up is the mechanism that keeps the A-PCT aligned towards its iteration goal and identifies potential obstacles. During it the Agile Team Members check the heartbeat of the project and get individual commitments from each other until the next checkpoint, usually twenty-four hours. It is neither a status update meeting nor a problem-solving meeting: issues raised are registered and discussed by the relevant team members immediately after the meeting.
meta: Sixty to ninety seconds per Agile Team Member
A team of ten ATeMs → maximum duration about fifteen minutes
Until the next checkpoint, usually twenty-four hours
ATeM Responsible and Accountable · ArOw also Responsible (acts as an ATeM here)
The Business Manager is marked N/A — the only ceremony where a role is not applicable
Individual commitments to the next checkpoint · the "meet after" list
§5.2, pp. 45–47 (RAM p. 47; Appendix B.2 p. 95, under Executing)

items: Not a status update meeting
Not a problem-solving meeting
Issues raised are registered, then discussed by the relevant team members immediately after the meeting

diagram.sec: 1. Each ATeM answers the four questions
items: What was I working on since the last checkpoint towards the iteration goal?
What will I be working on until the next checkpoint towards the iteration goal?
What blockers do I have that may prevent us from achieving the iteration goal?
How confident am I that we will accomplish the iteration goal?
Every question is framed against the iteration goal — that is what makes it alignment and not reporting
The Stand-up starts spontaneously when an ATeM takes the initiative and starts sharing
As she finishes, the next team member should follow
The TeCo ensures each ATeM has the chance to speak and that the guidelines are respected
Each ATeM should spend a few minutes preparing their communication beforehand
As information is shared, topics may emerge that need deeper analysis — especially if the iteration goal is jeopardised
The TeCo notes which ATeMs should participate and registers them for a "meet after"
The Parking Lot: a pre-defined space on the Kanban board, one post-it per topic with one or two names, to make the pendencies visible
After everyone has shared, the TeCo reminds the participants of their "meet after" so they can make the necessary arrangements
It is the Agile Team Members' sole responsibility to organise the "meet after", not the Team Coordinator's
By the end, the team can see the future activities and who is involved
Same time, same place — it is part of the A-PCT's daily routine
Prepare communication, even though the meeting is short
Keep everyone focused; when focus drifts the TeCo guides the ATeM back on track
Use a Kanban board — physical or digital — to illustrate what is being said
Use common sense: do not interrupt, listen carefully, be honest and transparent

diagram.sec: Who is where in the room
items: TeCo — supports, facilitates, consolidates the "meet after"
ATeM — responsible for execution; provides information on the work and its alignment with the team and the goal
ArOw — in this particular case, acts like a regular Agile Team Member
PrOw — informed of the outcomes only if necessary
PM — is informed about the outcomes of the Daily Stand-up
BM — N/A

fields.what: Keep the A-PCT aligned towards the iteration goal and identify potential obstacles; members check the project's heartbeat and take commitments from each other.
fields.pollux: 09:30 every working day in the Kirchberg team room, standing.

fields.what: "What was I working on since the last checkpoint towards the iteration goal?" Work is reported against the goal, not against a task list.
fields.pollux: Babbage: the nightly instrument reference sync, first of two 8-hour tasks.

fields.what: "What will I be working on until the next checkpoint towards the iteration goal?" This is the individual commitment the others rely on.
fields.pollux: Lamarr: the drill-through API contract for WIL-127.

fields.what: "What blockers do I have that may prevent us from achieving the iteration goal?" Blockers are named, not solved, in the meeting.
fields.who: Each ATeM raises · A-PCT resolves after
fields.pollux: Babbage: the sync window still collides with the lending-platform batch.

fields.what: "How confident am I that we will accomplish the iteration goal?" The daily echo of the Vote of Confidence taken at Iteration Planning.
fields.pollux: Babbage answered 2 on 05 Apr — the earliest warning that WIL-127 would slip.

fields.what: The interval between stand-ups against which commitments are made — usually twenty-four hours.
fields.pollux: Daily; POLLUX has no Friday-only or three-times-a-week variant.

fields.what: Sixty to ninety seconds per ATeM as a rule of thumb; with ten ATeMs the maximum duration should be about fifteen minutes.
fields.pollux: Four speakers, so the stand-up closes inside eight minutes.

fields.what: The ceremony exists for peer alignment, not for reporting upwards. Status for the managing layer travels via the Development Status Report.
fields.pollux: The PM's Release 2 status question was deferred to the status report.

fields.what: Issues raised are registered and then discussed by the relevant team members immediately after the meeting, not during it.
fields.pollux: The batch-window debate lasted ten seconds, then moved to the meet after.

fields.what: The Stand-up starts when an ATeM takes the initiative and starts sharing; as she finishes, the next member follows. No chairperson calls on people.
fields.pollux: Eiffel usually opens; the order is never fixed.

fields.what: A follow-up session for a topic needing deeper analysis. The TeCo notes who should attend and registers it, and reminds participants at the end.
fields.pollux: 05 Apr: Babbage + Einstein, batch window, ten minutes at the board.

fields.what: It is the Agile Team Members' sole responsibility to organise it — explicitly not the Team Coordinator's.
fields.pollux: Lovelace names it and stops; Babbage books the room.

fields.what: A pre-defined space on the Kanban board where the TeCo posts each pendency — topic plus one or two names — so future activities and owners are visible.
fields.pollux: Two post-its on 05 Apr: batch window, and Finance sign-off.

fields.what: The visual support for the Stand-up: each ATeM should materialise her communication using elements from the board wherever possible.
fields.pollux: Iteration 7 board columns mirror the WIL states plus the Parking Lot.

fields.what: Holding it in the same place and time consolidates the daily routine and lets participants organise their agendas around it.
fields.pollux: 09:30, team room B4 — unchanged since iteration 1.

fields.what: In this particular ceremony the Architecture Owner acts like a regular Agile Team Member and carries an R in the RAM.
fields.pollux: Einstein answers the four questions like everyone else.

fields.what: The Product Owner is informed about the outcomes of the meeting only if necessary. Attendance is not the point of the ceremony.
fields.pollux: Curie attends about twice a week and never speaks first.

fields.what: The Project Manager is informed about the outcomes of the Daily Stand-up. The ceremony is not a channel for the PM to collect updates.
fields.pollux: Conflict logged in iteration 7: the PM began attending and asking for updates.

fields.what: The RAM prints N/A for the Business Manager — the role has no part in this ceremony at all, which is different from being Informed.
fields.pollux: Hopper hears iteration progress at the Review, not at the stand-up.

traps: The BM is N/A here, not I — the only N/A in the ceremony RAMs.
The ArOw is R in the Stand-up, unlike the S it holds elsewhere.
The "meet after" is organised by the ATeMs, never by the TeCo.
Fifteen minutes is a consequence of ten members, not a fixed timebox.
A PM collecting status turns the Stand-up into the thing the guide forbids.
